answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with a narrow onboarding bridge: only a fixed handful of new agents enter each epoch, and each must first complete a public task on the open mesa of past work where established peers inspect it. Every newcomer carries a lantern that starts dim and brightens only after repeated, independently verified contributions. Spawning a hundred clones yields a hundred dim lanterns that cannot clear the entry quota, so an attacker must pay real time and verified work for each identity instead of minting them free.
